route-des-grandes-alpes-galibier-stage.title: Route des Grandes Alpes · Galibier Stage
route-des-grandes-alpes-galibier-stage.slogan: 3 passes in 111 km, topping out at 2642 m
route-des-grandes-alpes-galibier-stage.story: The Galibier is the centrepiece of the Route des Grandes Alpes: a long, exposed climb over 2600 m with the Télégraphe as its warm-up. The surface is good, the gradients are steady, and the traffic is mostly other people who came for the same thing. Snow can keep the top shut into June.

waypoints.name: Saint-Michel-de-Maurienne
waypoints.advice: Saint-Michel-de-Maurienne is where the day begins. Next is Col du Télégraphe, climbing 854 m.

waypoints.name: Col du Télégraphe
waypoints.advice: You top out at 1566 m here. The road climbs 854 m on the way up to it, steadily. Reckon on about 6 °C colder than the valley, and more in the wind. High enough to hold ice in the shaded corners early and late in the year. Next is Valloire.

waypoints.name: Valloire
waypoints.advice: A break here. Reckon on about 5 °C colder than the valley, and more in the wind. Next is Col du Galibier, climbing 1212 m.

waypoints.name: Col du Galibier
waypoints.advice: The high point of this section, 2642 m up. The road climbs 1212 m on the way up to it, hard. Reckon on about 13 °C colder than the valley, and more in the wind. Nothing on this route is higher. At this height the road is a summer one: snow gates can stay shut into June and shut again in October. Next is Col du Lautaret, mostly downhill.

waypoints.name: Col du Lautaret
waypoints.advice: Col du Lautaret tops the climb at 2058 m. You lose 584 m on the way down to it, steadily. Reckon on about 9 °C colder than the valley, and more in the wind. Next is Briançon, mostly downhill.

waypoints.name: Briançon
waypoints.advice: Briançon comes up 93 km in. You lose 732 m on the way down to it, steadily. Reckon on about 4 °C colder than the valley, and more in the wind. Next is back to Saint-Michel-de-Maurienne, mostly downhill.

waypoints.name: back to Saint-Michel-de-Maurienne
waypoints.advice: back to Saint-Michel-de-Maurienne closes the day. You lose 614 m on the way down to it, steadily.

route-des-grandes-alpes-galibier-stage.speedBand: Posted limits vary by country - read the signs, not the app

scenicChapters.title: Route des Grandes Alpes
scenicChapters.narrative: The last of the trees go and the road runs out onto open ground. The summit sits at 2642 m, and what surrounds it is rock, weather and distance — cold comes early up here and stays late. Ride it with something in reserve: the summit is not the end of the work, only the middle of it.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

scenicChapters.title: Route des Grandes Alpes
scenicChapters.narrative: 50 km that neither climbs nor drops much. The road settles into the ground rather than fighting it. This is where a day makes up time without anyone trying. Third and fourth, and very little else.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

scenicChapters.title: Parco Nazionale delle Incisioni Rupestri d → Fiavé-Lago Carera
scenicChapters.narrative: Slow enough to look. The surface follows the shoreline, so the corners arrive where the water decided, not where an engineer did. Water arrives beside the road and stays for 50 km. The line follows the shore because there is nowhere else for it to go.

places-segment-juli-cruz-pata-ccaje-segm.story: A 297 km round trip from Juli - roughly 5 h 07 in the saddle. The stops in between: Segment Desaguadero Titijoni, Segment Kallamarka-Apacheta and back through Segment Desaguadero Titijoni. The highest point is about 4,150 m. It crosses from Peru into Bolivia - carry ID and check vignette or toll rules. It was put together for the scenery rather than the shortest line.
